title: Euler with reversed stretching
premise_risks: arXiv:2602.13963 (2026 preprint, cited in refs): background on 1D/sign-of-stretching models only; the statement does not depend on it.
plain: Flip the sign of the vortex-stretching term in the 3D Euler vorticity equation and keep advection and the Biot-Savart law. Do smooth solutions stay smooth forever, or can they blow up in finite time? Unlike Euler, this equation does not preserve div ω = 0, so for t > 0 the vorticity ω need not equal curl u. The velocity u is always given by the stated Biot-Savart law (which sees only the divergence-free part of ω), and the question concerns this system as written.
